translations.text: She deceives herself and many senseless people, like animals, [?] the Scriptures.
Only because of pride, as I said before,
and disobedience, all these multitudes are going down to the underworld, whether men or women. For it was also because of pride and disobedience, as we said before,
that the devil was thrown out of heaven at the beginning.
Who, then, can count, or has counted from the beginning, those who have perished and gone down into the pit?
For they walked on the path of pride and lived in a state of [?].
For after everything the Lord had said from the beginning, whether in parables or plainly, the last of all his sayings was this:
“Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.” Does not everyone have ears? Or has a human being ever existed without ears?
Does not the Creator of everything, Christ the King, know that he has never created a human being without ears?
And what is this saying that he spoke: “Let whoever has ears listen”?
But since he knows that the pride within people is an abomination before God, as he said,
he therefore said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear,” because of disobedience
and pride, about which Scripture said, “My people did not listen to my voice,
and Israel paid no attention to me.
I sent them away according to the desires of their hearts.
They will walk in their own deeds.” And again, it was because of pride and disobedience that the Lord said in anger,
“I brought forth wonders; I raised them.
But they rejected me. An ox knows its owner, and a donkey knows its master's feeding trough.
But Israel has not known me, and my people have not discovered who I am.” And again, it was because of pride and disobedience that the Lord threatened these people at that time,
saying, “I sent you all my servants, the prophets, by day and early in the morning.
I sent them, but they did not listen to them, nor did their ears pay attention.
Instead, they followed the thoughts of their evil hearts.”
Again, because of pride, Scripture has expressed indignation against these people from the beginning,
saying, “The sin of their mouth,
the words of their lips—let them be caught in their pride.
They will proclaim their end through their curse.” We have said these things knowing that, just as the love of money is the root of every evil, according to the words of the Scriptures,
This, too, is how disobedience is the root of every evil,
according also to the words of the Scriptures—especially those who harbor hatred toward their neighbors without cause, committing their murders in their hearts instead of with their hands.
The Lord spoke with Adam at the beginning, establishing a covenant with him when he created him, placing all creation on earth into his hands and those of his offspring.
And he establishes an everlasting covenant with him and his descendants, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and rule over it.
Fear and dread of you will fall upon all the wild beasts, all the animals of the field, all the birds of the sky, and all the fish of the sea.
I have placed them in your hands. They will be food for you; just like the green plants, I have given them to you.
But you must not eat raw flesh with its lifeblood.
For I will also demand an accounting for the blood of your lives.
I will demand an accounting for it from the hand of every wild beast.” Will God, then, judge the wild beasts?
Or do wild beasts actually have hands, as he said,
“I will demand an accounting for it from the hand of the wild beasts”?
Rather, God knows from the beginning that many people will change into the nature of wild beasts by allowing the devil to dwell within them, so that he carries out his murders within them.
This is what Cain did without delay, just as he continued by saying, “Whoever sheds a person's blood,
his own blood will be shed in return.” Truly, according to the words of the Scriptures,
there are many people whom wild beasts surpass in goodness. For wild beasts, this is their nature.
But the people who have changed and acquired the heart of a wild beast—it is not their nature.
Or again, Scripture will tell us that there are many people who outwardly take on a human appearance but inwardly are wild beasts.
They are like the devil, who takes on the appearance of an angel of light, although he is darkness,
and he is a murderer.
For Paul also wrote about the people of Crete, “They are always liars; they are evil beasts;
they are lazy bellies.” Again, describing the full extent of the deeds of people who have changed from their own nature into the nature of wild beasts,
he says, “If, in human terms, I fought with wild beasts in Ephesus.”
Did the holy apostle, then, fight with actual wild beasts in Ephesus?
Rather, they were people who behaved like wild beasts instead of human beings.
When Jesus, the Lord of glory, speaks with his holy apostles, he says about those who behave like wild beasts instead of human beings,
“Look, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves.
So be wise like snakes.
And be innocent like doves. Guard yourselves against people who have the nature of beasts rather than human beings.
For they will hand you over to councils, and they will flog you in their synagogues.”
For the race of those beasts will not disappear until the end of the age.
And neither will the race of the blessed sheep of the flock of the good shepherd, Christ, disappear until the end of the age.
Especially that sort of people who live in idleness, according to what is written: “Every idle person is full of desires.”
If Scripture said, “Be still and know that I am God,” it does not permit each person to refrain from working for their livelihood, food, and clothing.
Rather, it says, “Cease from the works of the flesh,” which are sexual immorality, idol worship, sorcery, hostilities, quarrels, jealousy, contentiousness, divisions, factions, and slanders.
drunkenness, revelry, and things like these.
Those who practice these things will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
Nor will they know that God is God, as Scripture said.
“Be still and know that I am God.” For unless a person stops,
or ceases doing lawless deeds,
he cannot do righteous deeds,
as the Lord said: “No one can serve two masters.
For either he will love one and hate the other, or he will attach himself to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and Mammon.”
If the Lord also said, when speaking with the Jews at that time, “Do not work for food that will perish, but for food that will last forever,”
the king and the king’s son is not speaking—
God and the Son of God—about food and clothing to prevent a person from working for the things he needs, so that we will not become a burden
or a hardship to one of you, requiring you to provide for us from what belongs to you. How, then, now
can anyone say that he can maintain his livelihood securely without working, when the Lord commanded Adam from the beginning, when he placed him in paradise, to work in it and guard it?
For he did not leave him without work or without guarding the fruits of his labor so that they would be safe for him, as it is written:
“With every precaution, guard your heart,
for paths of life come from these.”
And after he cast him out of paradise, he did not leave him idle, without working.
Instead, he said to him, “You will eat the plants of the field by the sweat of your face,”
and, “You will eat your bread until you return to the earth.” With which people has God ever found fault, from the beginning,
because they work for their food and clothing? Rather, Scripture has found fault from the beginning, saying:
“For we hear about some among you who behave in a disorderly way, doing no work at all, but being busybodies.”
We therefore command people like these in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread. Or, “Do not let someone who does not work eat.”
Or who among all the holy people is there whom Scripture does not point out,
describing the work of each one and setting them before us as examples through their work? Cain and Abel, the first to be born—did not each one become a shepherd, and did not each one work the land?
God did not find fault with Abel because he tended the sheep,
nor was he angry with Cain because he worked the land.
But it was Cain’s lawlessness that disgraced him.
And it was Abel’s righteousness that justified him. And again, Noah, with whom the Lord spoke:
“For you are the one whom I have seen to be righteous before me in this generation.”
Scripture testifies about him, saying, “Noah was a farmer.
He began to plant a vineyard.”
Then again, the great Abraham, with whom God established a covenant, to multiply his descendants like the stars of heaven
and like the sand on the seashore, which cannot be counted, and that his descendants should inherit the cities of their enemies,
and that all the nations should be blessed through him, as we know that the old covenant and the new came into being through him and his descendants.
And we find it written about him that Abraham planted a tree [?] beside the Well of the Oath.
He called on the name of the Lord in that place, saying, “The everlasting God.” Or if Abraham had not been a sower
and a reaper, would he himself have planted beside the Well of the Oath after he finished establishing a covenant with Abimelech, as it is written about him,
“Abraham was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold”?
Then did not Lot lift up his eyes and see that the entire region of the Jordan was well watered, and settle there with his livestock,
because they were numerous?
He was the one whom God rescued from the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, together with his wife and his children.
Or is it not written about Isaac that he sowed in that year
and obtained a hundred measures of barley?
Then again, Jacob, whom God blessed because of his father Abraham and Isaac—does he not himself say:
“I burn in the heat of the day and in the frost of the night.
Sleep has departed from my eyes.”
Or, “Look, for twenty years now I have been tending your sheep.”
Did the Lord withhold his blessing and fail to bless him? Or did he not multiply his descendants because he was in the countryside all the time?
Not only did God bless him, but his angels were also with him among the sheep,
as they appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Lift up your eyes and look at the white-skinned rams, the black ones, and the spotted ones,
and the reddish, star-speckled ones [?], mounting the sheep and the goats.
For I have seen what Laban is doing to you.”
Indeed, not only were the angels with him among the sheep, but they also walked with him on the road, guiding him as he went up to Canaan, the land where he was born,
just as Jacob lifted up his eyes and saw God’s camp coming toward him.
And the angels of God met him.
When he saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.”
And he named that place “The Camp.”
Or who rebuked Laban as he rushed against him with a sword in his hand,
he and his brothers, saying, “Be careful not to say anything evil to Jacob”?
As Laban said to Jacob when he met him, “You carried off my children like prisoners taken by the sword.
You did not allow us to kiss my sons and daughters. Now you have acted foolishly.
“And now I have the power to harm you, but the God of your father said to me yesterday, ‘Be careful not to speak to Jacob
with evil words.’” Likewise, Jacob himself also spoke to Laban when he was arguing with him: “If the God of my father Abraham had not been on my side,”
and the Fear of Isaac, you would now have sent me away empty-handed.
But God saw my humiliation and the toil of my hands.
He rebuked you yesterday.”
We said these things so that we might understand that not only do the angels walk with him, but the Lord is also not far from him, being with him wherever he goes,
just as he also spoke with him elsewhere, when he appeared to him as he was going down to Egypt with him:
“And I myself will bring you back up, and Joseph will lay his hand upon your eyes.” Then again, the sons of Jacob,
whose descendants God made like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore, which cannot be counted.
Were they not in the fields tending their father's sheep? As Jacob called Joseph,
he sent him, saying, “Go and see whether your brothers and the sheep are well, and bring me news of them.” He sent him out from the valley of Hebron.
Now he had come down to Shechem, and a man found him wandering in the fields and asked him, “Who are you looking for?”
He said, “I am looking for my brothers. Tell me where they are tending their flocks.”
He said to him, “For I heard them say, ‘Let us go down to Dothan.’”
We said these things because God will not dishonor a person for being in the fields doing his work for his food and clothing, while pleasing God.
Nor will he honor a person for being secluded as an ascetic while remaining idle, without working with his hands, especially when he does not please God through good works
and good deeds. Rather, it is fitting for the person in the fields to please God, so that God will bless him
and also bless the produce of his land.
It is also right for someone who has committed himself as a monk and an ascetic to work with his hands
for his food and clothing, and to do God's will through godly deeds, so that he may receive a blessing from the Lord upon the earth.
and find mercy before God on the day of his visitation.
For we say these things so that we might understand that God loves everyone who fears him and puts his hope in his name, and everyone who works with his hands so that he may have possessions.
[?] money, sexual immorality, theft, lying, and false oaths are evident in the person who commits them.
Those near him and those who live with him often recognize him or catch him. But the person who hates his neighbor,
or the person who envies his neighbor—these things are inside the heart and are not evident to those near them and those who live with them.

But just as the devil is hidden with his demons of darkness in the things he does out of hatred for the whole human race, so too is the person who envies his neighbor and hates him: his evil deeds are hidden within him.
Day and night are darkness to him in the chambers of his heart, because his deeds are not evident.
Because of my sin, the Holy Spirit said, knowing that [?]
more than all acts of lawlessness, concerning those who do these things: “The person who speaks peaceful words to his neighbor while hostility, jealousy, and hatred are in his heart.”
give them according to their deeds and according to the wickedness of their thoughts.
Give them their repayment.” He will indeed give it to them. Or what is their repayment? He will put upon them the curse they loved
and make it a crown upon their heads.
[?] words [?]
You will tear them down and not build them up.
Oh, blessed are you, love for humanity! You are adorned on every side
with the virtues of the Spirit, as you go before Christ to receive according to your worth in the places of rest in heaven.
“For his appearance is not the appearance of a human being.”
But [?]
The rejection of people, deceit,
rejoicing over your neighbor’s destruction—but the Scripture of God stands against it.
And the things she said from the beginning about those who do these things, to send her down and wipe her out,
like those who do not exist, at the time and hour when she will give her spirit into the hands of the one who hates her.
Christ, along with all its other bitter deeds, as it is written: “The person who rejoices over someone who is going to perish will not escape evil.”
For indeed, when the Lord became a human being among human beings—God and the Son of God—

he is the one who commanded Adam in paradise not to eat from the tree. He is the one who commanded Abraham and his household to undergo circumcision of the flesh. He is the one who spoke with Moses at the bush,
having performed all these miracles through his staff, about which he spoke to Moses, saying, “Take this staff in your hand,
with which you will perform all these signs.” He went on to carry them out before Pharaoh and all the Egyptians,
by the power of his arm, as it is written: “The one who brought Israel out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand and an uplifted arm.”
He is the one who gave the law to Moses in the wilderness, and the one through whom every commandment and every law came into being.
He is the one who did these things, having done far, far more than what we have said, for there is no limit to his mighty deeds.
And there is no end to his wonders. So when he became human among human beings, he was God and the Son of God.
an expert in the law approached him.
He questioned him, testing him: “What is the greatest commandment in the law?”
The true Savior, Jesus, answered him.
“Hear, Israel: the Lord your God is one.
You shall love the Lord
your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your thoughts,
and your neighbor as yourself.” He answered him, “Well
you have spoken: God is one, and there is no other besides him.
And you shall love him with all your heart, with all your strength, and with all your understanding.
This,” he said, “is better than all the burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
And when the Lord of glory realized that he had honored love for humanity as it deserved, he granted him the kingdom of heaven without hesitation,
saying, “You too are not far from the kingdom of heaven.”
But he wanted to understand the perfection of love for humanity, so that he would receive greater honor.
He asked him, “Who is my neighbor?” The King of the powers answered him, teaching him the perfection of the straight path: “A man went out from Jerusalem toward Jericho.
He fell into the hands of some [?] robbers. They stripped him and wounded him.
They went away and left him half dead.
By chance, a priest was going down that road.
He saw him and passed him by.
But a Samaritan came down that road, saw him, and had compassion on him.
He approached him and bandaged his wounds.
He poured wine and oil over him and put him on his own animal.
He brought him to an inn and took care of him. The next day, as he was leaving, he gave [?] coins.
To the innkeeper, saying to him, “Take care of him.”
“And whatever you spend on him, I will give you when I return.” Who among these three
He said, “The one who became a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of the robbers?”
He said to him, “It was the one who showed him mercy.”
Then the Lord of glory, Jesus, said to him, “Go, and you too do likewise.”
So that we may understand that we have said nothing different in what we have said outside Scripture, and also so that we may understand that love is love for humanity, and love for humanity is love.
If he granted this man the kingdom because he spoke the truth in his answer—that love for humanity is better than all the burnt offerings and sacrifices
Then the one who will also fulfill it within his heart
and all its other righteous deeds—how greatly will he honor him?
And how will he grant him the kingdom of heaven?
So let us not boast, brothers, that we are Christians while there is jealousy, strife, or hatred in our hearts toward our neighbor.
Or if we do not love our neighbor as ourselves,
we are not perfect in our deeds.
The name by which we are called is nothing but an empty name.
The holy apostle cries out: “For since there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not worldly?
And are you not living according to human ways?”
What, then, will we say on the day when we are called to account, if we have not recognized what we are like before the days of our lives come to an end?
We will mourn in the place of mourning, where many have mourned since the beginning of the world.
And we will weep in the place of weeping, where many have wept since the beginning.
If it is because of you, O love for humanity and love, that this whole multitude will receive glory when the King comes
in his glory, with all his angels with him, as we said before,
and they will enter eternal life,
blessed are you, and blessed is the Lord of glory, Jesus, because he has sown you for himself in the hearts of the wise,
so that they may inherit life forever, with every honor and all glory, with great confidence in heaven,

And if it is because of you, in turn, O hatred of humanity, that this entire multitude and these numerous peoples, from the beginning of the world until now and until the end of the age, will receive disgrace,
when the King comes in his glory to judge between these and the others, between those on the right because of love and mercy
and perfect love for humanity, and those on the left because of envy and hatred and mercilessness.
then cursed is the one who spread you,
the devil, who sowed you for himself as an evil seed in the hearts of the foolish.
For it is he, the dragon, who fought against you with the abundance of poisons coming from his mouth, until he led very many astray without their realizing that he had led them astray
from the road leading to the city where they were to live, having brought them out of the light into darkness, without their realizing that it was darkness.
in which they are walking, according to what is written:
“Whoever hates his brother is in darkness and walks in darkness.
He does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.”
Until they hear this voice, full of wrath, coming from the mouth of the Almighty, Jesus, as he calls them to account for what they ought to have done,
according to the decree of judgment written in the Gospels.
This is what he foretold to us—the one who does not wish anything in his creation to perish—saying, “This is how I will act
when I come, according to what those on the right deserve, according to their deeds in every kind of love for humanity.
And again: “This is the decree concerning those on the left when he comes, according to what they deserve:
Receive now, you wretched, miserable people, together with the one you loved and with whom you worked in envy and hatred
and in utter mercilessness, down in the fire of Gehenna, not for days and years, but forever and ever.”
For these things will happen at the end of the age, and there will be no further judgment after this.
And there will no longer be a day to look forward to for resurrection, after he has judged the angels and passed judgment on the full extent of every lawless deed,
and sends them down to Hades in the fury of his wrath, whether those among the angels whom he deceived or those among human beings whom he led astray.
The angels will drive them all away:
everyone entangled in the lawless deeds of the son of destruction, who did not repent before they died, nor [?] leave those deeds before the day they were called to account.
In short, once and for all, everyone standing on the left will be thrown down into Hades and inherit the Gehenna of fire forever.
Oh, what turmoil there will be on that day for those standing on the left, before those on the right who are in glory!
Oh, what weeping there will be on that day among all the nations that did not know God,
and all the heretics, each one separately in the error into which deceit led them astray,
But people who say of themselves, “We are Christians,” will be in great misery and great distress on that day,
because they did not recognize the calling with which they were called, or the grace that reached them.
especially those who bear the name and wear the garb and live in the holy places,
they too being mixed with these in that wrath, because they did not listen to the voice of the Scriptures, which went out over the whole earth:
and their life-giving words, which reached the ends of the inhabited world, crying out, “Flee from sexual immorality!”
“Every sin a person commits,” it says, “is outside the body.
But the person who commits sexual immorality sins against their own body.”
Or: “The person who joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her.”
“But the person who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with him.” Or: “Do you not know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit lives in you?” Or: “Whoever defiles God's temple—
God will destroy that person.”
What, then, will happen after their outcry and after the groaning of those on the left in great fear, with the ministering angels,
flames of fire, turned toward them, while the sentence of Jesus the Almighty comes out of his mouth, pursuing them with wrath and terror:
“Depart from me,
“You who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels,
because you did not act according to what I commanded you, not merely because you did not love your neighbor because the task was difficult for you.
why, instead, did you hate him, turning justice into gall and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness?
You twisted what I told you into things I did not tell you, in every kind of lawlessness.
Receive now according to what you deserve and according to the wickedness of your deeds,
down in the fire of Gehenna, together with the one who turned your will into hatred and your love into mercilessness,
and your purity into defilement and sexual immorality in various forms that are loathsome to mention and shameful to hear about,
the one who turned complete godliness into complete ungodliness of every kind during your days on earth.”
You did not listen to me as I cried out through the mouths of my servants.”
The prophets: “Return to me so that you may live”—those from the beginning of the world.
Or, “Return to me, and I will heal your brokenness.” Or, “Come out from among them and separate yourselves from them.”
And I will welcome you, for I am merciful,” or, “I will be your God, and you will be my people.”
And, “I will be your Father, and you will be my sons and daughters.”
For if the one who is pure and those who are being purified all come from one, according to the Scriptures—that is, from God—
So the defiled one, the devil, and those who defile themselves all come from one, namely him—whether a demon or any of the unclean, deceitful spirits that are with him;
whether prostitutes or men who are worthless in every way, they all come from him, the devil—everyone who sins in any way.
What, then, will happen after the execution of the judgment of the Almighty Jesus and the Son of the Almighty Sabaoth is finished, as he sits upon the cherubim,
with the shining seraphim standing before him, together with the holy archangels, with great glory, and all his saints, as it is written: “The saints are the ones who will judge the world”?
And they will cast all those on the left down into hell with the devil, and seal him in with them and seal them in with him.
What, then, does remembering these things from this moment mean before God?
Oh, the great anguish and the great sorrow of anyone who understands these things that will happen on that day!
For we did not obey the Scriptures, but forgot and cast their words behind us.
taking on insensitivity and negligence until these things befall us, although we did not want them to befall us,
and until we find ourselves in these circumstances, although we did not want to be in them. Did not the Lord say,
“Everything you want people to do for you, you yourselves also
must do for them in the same way.
For this is the Law and the Prophets”?
Indeed, the good Savior did not hide the matter from us and fail to tell us: “The gate is wide,
and the road leading to destruction is spacious.”
Nor did he forget to tell us about the other one: “It is narrow and constricted.”
Furthermore, continuing to strengthen the practice of love for humanity and to put envy and hatred to shame,
He says, “But I tell you: Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
so that you may become children of your Father in heaven. For he makes his sun rise upon the good and the evil, and he sends rain upon the righteous and the wrongdoers.
For if you love those who love you,” he said, “what reward do you have?
Do not the tax collectors themselves do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing than the other Gentiles?”
They do not do this.
“Therefore, be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.”
The holy John the Baptist cried out from the beginning, since he had sent
him ahead of himself to guide the people toward love for humanity and love,
Since among all the virtues there is none greater than these, when the crowd came out to receive baptism from him, they asked him, “What should we do?”
He told them, “Let anyone who has two garments give one to someone who has none, and let anyone who has bread do likewise.”
And the holy apostle, whom the Lord sent to proclaim the gospel,
He cries out, saying, “Let brotherly love
continue.
Do not forget hospitality, for through it some have welcomed angels without knowing it.”
What, then, is greater than love for humanity, as we have said many times? And love is very exalted,
for mercy is its clothing, and the fulfillment of the commandments of life
is a crown upon its head. It greatly frightens its enemies as it goes to stand before God.
And the devil always trembles before her, filled with shame in her presence, when he sees the likeness of Christ clothing her, and the sign of his holy cross.
For it was because of his love for humanity and his mercy toward humankind that he endured the cross.
For when he finds fault through the prophet,
he speaks threateningly about people of this kind, whose hearts are full of deceit while they speak pleasantly to their neighbors.
There is indeed wrath before God against those who conduct themselves this way. How far, then, does their judgment reach? It reaches to the depths of Hades.
Since we have spoken about the prophet,
He says in his furious anger, as we said before, “Look, I will refine them.”
Where, then, will he refine them? “And I will test them, for I will act in the face of the wickedness of the daughter of my people.”
Their tongue is an arrow that strikes.
The words of their mouths are deceitful. They speak peaceful words to their neighbors, but hostility and hatred are in their hearts. Shall I not, for these things,
punish them?” says the Lord. “Or shall my soul not take vengeance on a nation like this?”
So that we may know that all the words of Scripture oppose this practice from the beginning.
The Old Testament and the New Testament. Now, since we have learned everything—our death and our life, our fullness and our lack, our going into God's presence rightly
by wisely observing what he has said, and our going down to Hades by foolishly transgressing what he has said—
let us therefore now consider these things and the others, before the day comes that we do not know,
and the hour that we do not recognize, and we receive according to our deeds, each one according to what he deserves and according to the fruit of his deeds.
Oh, blessed are the people because of whom God will be glorified through their good deeds, which are the sweet fragrance of Christ!
Oh, woe to the people because of whom their parents’ name will be disgraced through their lack of instruction!
The true and good Savior commands, “Do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing
“Whenever you perform an act of mercy”—and what he said is good.
Elsewhere, again revealing the deeds of a good person, he says, “Let them see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.”
So, then, there is no way for a person's good deeds to remain hidden.
For it is like a person who has fragrant perfume beneath his garment, without greatly [?] it outwardly:
he cannot restrain its fragrance and prevent people from smelling the fragrance within him whenever he passes them.
In the same way, no one who performs good deeds and good works before God can hide them so that people do not learn about them.
Whether it is night or day, he cannot hide them, according to what the Lord said: “Nothing is hidden that will not be revealed.”
Again, it is like a person who has a great stench within him: he gives off a very strong foul smell unwillingly, and he does not want people to smell it when he passes them.
But it is unavoidable, because it gives off an even greater stench. This is how it is with a person who does deeds
that do not please God and are detestable in people's eyes, even if he does them at night, in the darkness.
They must be revealed, as the apostle said: “Those that are otherwise cannot remain hidden.”
Strive, then, my beloved brothers, so that we may accomplish the work for which we have gathered together: purification and the other commandments given to us by God
through our holy father, so that we may receive honor on earth before both good and evil people.
And also so that we may be given even greater honor in heaven before God and all the saints.
And so that we may receive the reward for the good deeds we have done on earth, in the heavenly capital, Jerusalem, which is full of every good thing.
For our holy father Apa Athanasius says, “Preserve the honorable human likeness, for they will not call you a human being,” he said, “if you do the deeds of irrational creatures.”
Now then, beloved brothers, dear to the Lord, we have great pride in you everywhere we go, boasting about you,
as people tell us about your former deeds, saying, “Here is a people who are chosen and adorned
with wisdom, who fear God and also keep their fathers' commandments. We hear of no war among them
or sound of war; instead, they make their faith known everywhere.” Do outsiders live with us, so that they would know how each one of us
conducts himself in his deeds? Rather, they see the [?] around us and its fragrance—the righteousness of our fathers—which shines around our congregation,
shining brighter than the sun and giving off a fragrance greater than all perfumes. Because of this, they honor us even more and add to our good reputation.
If we have done a little, they will proclaim much more, and they tell one another about many good deeds, saying, “We do them.”
Truly, we feel ashamed and become as nothing in comparison with what people outside say about us.
Now then, brothers, let us be firm, like a city whose walls are strong and whose gates are shut.
For the Scriptures say, “Like a city whose walls have been torn down,
so is a person who does not act with counsel.”
What counsel, then, does Scripture speak about, other than the counsel of God? As it is written:
“There are many thoughts in a person's heart,
but it is God's counsel that stands firm.”
“A human being is great,” he said, “and a merciful person is precious.”
I too, wretched and poor as I am, will put it this way:
“A human being is great, and a holy person is even more excellent.”
Let us therefore carry out the work of godliness in every respect, whether in all spiritual activities
or in bodily activity through our manual labor, so that we may receive a blessing from the Lord.
and mercy from God our Savior, and so that people may say of us:
“This is the generation of those who seek the Lord.”
Please, then, my beloved brothers, be diligent about the morning reading and the reading at evening, and about your morning and evening assemblies.
Carry them out fully and patiently, without being disturbed by the one who causes disturbance, for it is written:
“The one who troubles you will bear the judgment, whoever he is.”
Then the written word will call you blessed: “Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord has chosen as his own inheritance.”
And the word of Scripture will call you blessed still more: “Blessed are the people who know the shout of joy.”
Lord, they will walk in the light of your face, and they will rejoice in your name all day long.
They will be exalted through your righteousness, for you are the glory of their strength. Our horn will be exalted through your righteousness.
And so that you too may be able to speak confidently about yourselves on this basis: the Lord is our protector, and the Holy One of Israel is our king.
Oh, blessed are people like us, whom many mouths will call blessed on earth,
and whom the mouths of tens of thousands upon tens of thousands in the heavens will also call blessed.
Oh, truly, woe to people who live as we do in God's congregations, whom those on earth will call blessed,
while those in heaven—vast multitudes—disown them because of their deeds.
Woe to people about whom those on earth say, “They are the ones,” while those in heaven say about them, “They are not the ones.”
Woe to people who live in God's houses, his congregations and his holy places, about whom those on earth say,
“They are God's children,” while those in heaven say, “That is not so. Rather, they are children of darkness and enemies of God because of their evil deeds.”
Especially those who commit these evil deeds—defilements and pollutions—in Christ's houses, let alone those of the people on earth.
Especially since they will be hidden from those in heaven, according to what is written,
“What is crooked cannot be put in order,” and, “What is lacking cannot be counted.”
Oh, blessed are people who live as we do and trust in their purity, just as our holy father
said this many times in his holy letters.
Woe, woe to people for whom this is not the case, and who do not possess this in God's congregations.
Oh, blessed are people who place their hope in their own hope, knowing that it pleases God and is accepted by Christ because of their wisdom
and their good conduct, through which they have acquired for themselves a hope in heaven and indescribable wealth forever.
And woe to people who have no hope in heaven and do not know what it is that they trust in.
Why? Because of these deeds—these deeds again—because of their foolishness and their disobedience, since people like these have brought misery and poverty upon themselves.
and weeping and mourning forever down in the underworld.
Since, then, we have understood, brothers, what we ought to do during these few days that are swiftly passing away, as it is written by another holy man, “For my lifetime is swifter than a runner,”
let us not forget, nor let us be negligent, for we will not be given another day
when the days of each one of us have come to an end. If we speak, we will have much to say about the misery of those who will be negligent.
And again, if we speak, we will say much about those who will become rich through their diligence,
by setting their conduct right and healing themselves through repentance after they have fallen. For the work is open to everyone on earth at all times, to anyone who wishes to be saved.
But our willfulness and our disobedience are what make us unworthy of these things. For it is indeed written,
“Unless the Lord builds a house, those who build it have labored in vain.”
And, “Unless the Lord guards a city, its guardian has spent a night keeping watch in vain.”
Again, “No one can say, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ except through the Holy Spirit.”
And again, Jesus, the Lord of glory, says, “Without me you can do nothing.” Therefore, unless God works with a person,
that person cannot work toward his salvation on his own. For when a person works with God in virtuous conduct and good deeds,
God, in turn, works with him in every blessing and makes him grow in the fruits of righteousness.
Who has ever put his hope in God from the beginning and been abandoned by God, according to what we read?
Likewise, now he says, “I am he. I am he, and even when you grow old, I am still he.” Jesus Christ himself is the same yesterday,
and he is the same today, and also forever.
Oh, blessed are those who understand and come between good and evil: evil, so that they may guard themselves
against doing it; but good, so that they may carry it out cheerfully.
It is written,
for, “It is a cheerful giver whom God loves.”
What, then, is a giver? It is not merely someone who gives bread and clothing to his neighbor, but whatever you do among the works of righteousness, completing them joyfully,
whether prayer, ascetic discipline, purity of heart and purity of body—doing all these joyfully—or praising God by day and by night,
knowing for whom you do them, and also knowing from whom you will receive their reward. He knows.
that whoever approaches God must believe that he exists and that he will reward those who seek him.
So let us not neglect ourselves at sowing time, so that we may find something to reap or gather.
There are many people who toil without understanding how to watch over themselves. The written saying will be fulfilled in them: “Why do you toil,
and your labor brings no satisfaction?”
Thus there is nothing new under the sun. The things that have been tested
have been tested from the beginning,
and they were written down for us as instruction by those who taught,
and with whom the Lord spoke.
For I have already said this many times:
it is not just one sin that fights against a person, but very many.
Not only is hatred of people cursed, as has been written about it,
but oppression is even more cursed.
For this reason Scripture says, “Let everyone who utters the name of the Lord turn away from oppression.”
This, too, is how our holy father did not hold back his words about slander in his holy letters, saying these things and others:
“Woe to those who join one another in slander, running to one another with a strong desire to carry it out together!
I, this poor, wretched man, put it this way: just as those who run to one another with great burning desire, through the devil, wish to commit sexual immorality,
so also do those who run to one another to engage in slander.
For indeed, I have said these things many times because of the harm suffered by people of this kind, who destroy their hope.
at the same time, and wasting their efforts, with no benefit for them in all their toil because of their mouths and their ears.
Is it not written, “The person who says, ‘I am a worshiper of God,’ but does not bridle his tongue—his worship is worthless”?
For whoever takes part in slander and grumbling takes part in sexual immorality without knowing it. The man who commits sexual immorality
and the woman with whom he commits it look anxiously this way and that, so that people will not see them, until they have carried out their sexual acts.
Likewise, the person who slanders and the person who listens withdraw to one side by themselves, looking anxiously this way and that, lest someone hear them before they finish their slander.
For this reason, both groups are cursed together by God: those who practice sexual immorality and those who slander.
Indeed, the person who slanders is no different from the person who practices sexual immorality, and the person who practices sexual immorality is no different from the person who slanders.
For just as a person's heart is filled with defilement
and burns with desire for sexual immorality, and he has no way to carry it out according to his evil desires unless he finds a woman with whom to have illicit sex,
or else fulfills those desires in other unnatural ways with those whom he finds ready for their cursed practice, both these and the others,
so it is also with slander.
Even if the ungodly man's heart is full of its filth, he cannot carry out his impure acts with his mouth unless he finds someone like himself, under this same curse,
burning to hear about his neighbor's filth and disgrace,
For the listener will take delight like the prostitute who takes delight in pleasure with those who have illicit sex with her.
This is how the person who listens to slander wants the slanderer not to get up and leave him,
and not to stop speaking while insulting his neighbor. What, then, are these two people like?
The speaker and the listener are like Satan and lawlessness, and lawlessness and Satan. Or is the listener perhaps not worse than the slanderer?
This is how the listener looks out after the other man has gotten up and left him, having carried out all his sexual immorality with his mouth in the listener's ears,
like someone committing sexual immorality, carrying out all his sexual immorality with his mouth into the listener's ears,
like someone committing sexual immorality, carrying out all his sexual immorality in the lap of the wicked woman, who looks out with the burning desire of his wicked heart
to see whether someone else is also coming to tell him things, just as the one who got up told him.
So that he may take still greater pleasure in insulting many people who are better than he is, just like the prostitute who displays herself in the streets, serving as a snare.
A multitude of wretches! After this man gets up from beside her, having carried out his sexual immorality with her,
she looks for another, or for others, to see whom she will find who are like her, under this same curse,
this one and that other one, so that they may carry out acts of sexual immorality with her. Will people of this kind, then, ruin the labor of those who please God? It would be
better if people of this kind—the slanderer and the listener—had sought only their own glory and boasted in it,
all the more eager to seek out their neighbors' disgrace and the shame of their fellow servants of God,
since it is the same God whom they worship, and the same Lord whom they serve.
Still more, so that they may delight in a delight full of weeping without knowing it, and rejoice with a false joy over the humiliation of their neighbors, a joy full of grief, without realizing it.
What the devil desires is also what these people love, and what the demons rejoice over
is also what they rejoice in.
Indeed, our holy father himself said this in anger and wrath from God:
“It has been said about two kinds that they cast their lust into their mouths.
One kind,” he said, “is among the birds that are in the waters of the rivers, and the other is among the creeping creatures on the earth.”
“This is what this kind of person is like,” he said: “the one who slanders and the one who listens to him.”
What, then, is the portion of these people, or what is the lot of those others?
If all the words of anger that Scripture has spoken through God come down upon them: “I cast out the one who slanders
his neighbor secretly,” or, “You sat slandering your brother, and you laid a stumbling block for your mother's son.”
“You did these things, and I kept silent.”
“You thought [?]”
“that I would be like you.”
“I will rebuke you and set these things before you. Understand these things, then, you who forget God,” he said.
Recognize your disgrace now from these things, lest he tear you apart and there be no one to rescue you.
“A sacrifice of praise is what will honor me,” he said—not slander. Certainly not! “This is the way I will show you, so that I may [?] God’s salvation.”
Oh, then, what will happen if the words of Scripture stand against us at Christ’s judgment seat! For this is indeed how it will be.
Do you not know, you poor, miserable man, that what you sow will grow, and what you throw down into the earth will come up?
If the good Savior said, “The kingdom of heaven is like”
“a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field—this is indeed smaller than all the seeds.”
Then, when it grows, it becomes larger than the vegetables and becomes a large tree, so that the birds of the sky come and dwell beneath its branches.
In the same way, if you sow good fruit in the earth, it grows into much good fruit, sweet and beneficial to people.
So too, if you sow bad fruit in the earth,
it grows, becoming prickly and harming those who walk past. If you sow the seed of the [?] in the earth, does it not grow? And how does it grow?
It, and all the other good and choice trees in the garden—how their owner surrounds them with walls!
He fences them in and watches over their fruit, because they are good to eat and benefit people.
Likewise, the vineyard is protected because its wine is beneficial,
and because it brings joy to those who drink it, especially those who are sick.
But look also at the thorn shoots, when you plant them in the ground, and at weeds
and every harmful wild tree: how they grow without caretakers surrounding them with walls!
Nor do they look after their fruit. Instead, they already hurt those who touch them, and they have no need of fences around them.
Recognize the fruit of those who practice righteousness on earth from what we have said. And recognize also the fruit of those who practice lawlessness on earth from what we have said.
Since, then, the devil knows—and he is cunning—
that a person is victorious on the road by which he will go to the one who created him, he therefore does everything he can to deceive many through those who will obey him.
Oh, you are cursed, devil, because of this multitude of schemes, differing from one another, which you have put into your evil heart!

You have put their stench to work as they sink into the hearts of the foolish. Those who hate their own souls are not wise. Those who love their own souls—[?]—until you make them strangers to life. How many will you cast away, and how many will you leave?
But this is the mire, this very mire, that you have prepared for those who bear the name and wear the habit.
and those in the places of Christ, especially throughout the whole land among those who wish to devote themselves to God.
It is hidden and obscure to all your villages, just as idolatry and the heretics are too.
For you have darkened their hearts until you led them astray and made them blind, so that they would not know the God who created them.
I am speaking of hatred, slander, and envy, through which you have secretly enticed people.
Scripture cries out: “Anyone who slanders his brother or judges his brother slanders the law
and judges the law. But if you judge the law, then you are not someone who carries out the law.”
Truly, someone who slanders his neighbor resembles those guilty of many lawless deeds. He resembles the sexually immoral, as we said before,
and he resembles a thief in what he does. Just as a thief is ashamed
when he is caught, according to the words of Scripture, with the stolen property in his hand,
so too is a slanderer ashamed.
And the listener too—if the person being slandered comes upon them or hears them without their knowing, after they have completed all their wickedness
and the words of envy and hatred in their mouths. Let them look beside them
and see him standing there, listening to them without their knowing it. And let them look behind them and see him in everything they have said.
they did not realize how greatly it changes—
their face—and their heart melts, so that we may understand that the fate of the thief
is the fate of the slanderer and the listener.
If your face has changed and your heart has melted because the person you are slandering has heard you,
then how disturbed will you be, or how full of shame will your face be, when those you do not know come after you?
and bring you before the one you have never seen, Christ, to punish you according to your deeds? He is the one who loved humanity, the one who did not curse when he was cursed,
He who offered himself up as a holy sacrifice to his Father, not for one or two people, nor for just one nation,
but for the whole world—for those who wish to be saved—has given us confidence and enabled us to cry out to him at all times.
Recognize his speaking with you, O human being, and his love for all people alike,
just as he taught us to cry out to him and his Father when he taught us to pray, “Our Father who is in heaven.”
He did not tell you to say only “My Father,” but “Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
May your kingdom come.
May your will be done. Just as it is in heaven, may it also be done on earth.”
“Our bread for the coming day,” he said.
Again, he did not allow you to say, “My bread for the coming day, give it to me today,” but “Our bread for the coming day, give it to us today.”
“Forgive us our debts,” he said.
He did not tell you, “Forgive me what you hold against me.” He said, “As we too forgive those against whom we have something.”
You are alone in your prayer, but with your mouth you bear witness for many that they forgive those against whom they have something.
And do not lead us into temptation.
You are one person, yet you pray for many through what the Savior, who loves humanity, has put into your mouth.
But rescue us from the power of the evil one, for yours are the power and the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Then recognize Christ’s love, as we said before: he makes his entire creation one in their prayer, wanting us to love one another, whether in our living together or in our conduct,
Whether it is our going to church or our partaking of the body and blood of the Lord,
we are united in love and of one mind in Christ, praying for one another in love,
just as he taught us to pray, so that he may accept it from us, rescue us from the power of the evil one, and grant us the kingdom of heaven.
Let us let go of every grievance in our hearts against our neighbor, so that he may forgive us too,
so that we may not be liars in our prayer when we say, “Forgive us, as we too forgive those against whom we have something.”
And again: “If anyone has a grievance against another, just as Christ forgave you,
you too must do the same.” And again: “If you forgive people their sins, your Father in heaven will also forgive you your sins.
For if you do not forgive people their sins,” he said, “your Father will not forgive you your sins.”
What do we have now? Jealousies, hatreds, and slanders,
especially defilements, impurities, acts of violence, and greed for more land, along with all the other abominable deeds of the devil and his demons, while God and his Christ
unite us as his children in the kingdom of heaven, so that we may inherit with Christ for ages upon ages, in all glory and every blessing forever.
What are we now to the devil and his demons, that they should punish us with him down in Hades, in the fire of Gehenna and with the worm that never sleeps, although we do not come from him?
He does not come from us now, but we come from God.
For he is the one who breathed a breath of life into our faces, and we have become one with him through the body and blood of his holy Son,
whom he graciously gave us. We have become one as children united with the holy Trinity, whether small or great, male or female—everyone who partakes of the Lord’s body and blood.
We have become one with God,
not as gods—certainly not!
But as children of their holy Father, and as brothers of the blessed Christ, the King of heaven and earth,
in accordance with what he said with his truthful mouth: “Whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven”—
when they asked him, “Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak with you,” and the one speaking to him answered, “Who is my mother?”
and who are my brothers? For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and my sister and my mother.”
Since we have these promises, beloved,
let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of the flesh and the spirit, bringing purity to completion in the fear of God the Lord.
As the apostle said, we give no cause for stumbling in anything, so that no one may find fault with the ministry.
Just as he also said this:
Blessed are you, Lord God Almighty.
The Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who created everything through his holy, beloved Son.
You are blessed, Jesus Christ.
And blessed is the Holy Spirit, who takes counsel with his holy Father, for every blessing upon the earth,
and for all mercy and compassion upon the earth, and for patience and forbearance.
For if you do not forgive us, God Almighty, and if you do not cover our sins, Jesus Christ, we are of no worth before you,
nor will we appear before you at all.
But we beg you, God of hosts, who performed all these wonders in Israel from the beginning for the sake of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
to perform them again among us now, for the sake of your holy name and for the sake of your holy, beloved Son, Jesus, our Savior and our life.
Do not keep an account against us, for we are flesh, and
We are dust, according to what you said from the beginning to the first human being, Adam: “You are dust, and you will return to dust.”
Forgive us, for we are clay and the work of your hands. Have mercy on us, God of hosts.
Forgive us, for we are grass, according to what you said with your own mouth through your prophets: “All flesh is grass.”
You are the God of hosts, through whom every power exists. You are the one who created the earth as nothing, while those who inhabit it are like locusts before you.
They have been compared to spittle, and to a drop hanging from a bucket, and to the tilting of a balance, according to the words of your prophets.
O God of hosts and Lord of glory, Jesus, if you do not have compassion on us, who will have compassion on us? If you do not show us mercy, who will show us mercy?
For you know our powerlessness and our weakness, and the frailty of our body is not hidden from you. You are blessed, Lord, and you are holy.
And blessed is the name of your holy glory forever and ever.
John. Exposition.
In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, the Trinity of one substance, indivisible.
We believe in the begetting of the only-begotten Son from his Father before the foundation of the world. We believe in the birth of our Savior from the Virgin Mary, who is a virgin at all times.
We believe in the sufferings that our Savior endured for us upon the cross, which is full of salvation.
We believe in his resurrection from the dead.
We believe in his ascension into heaven.
We hope to receive forgiveness of our sins through his holy body and his true blood.
After they have finished this canon of the holy Apa John throughout the whole church, let them stop, knowing that it is there in its entirety.
The Lord gave it to us in a small book, written in the ancient [?].
We moved it to serve as a lasting memorial.
We placed it under the authority of our fathers in the desert, so that it would remain under the authority of the church of the Virgin Mary on the mountain, in the days when Father Menas
and my father Zechariah were its stewards, so that everyone who asks for this holy book of rules may receive it from them, find comfort in its words, and give it back to them.
So that this great and perfect archimandrite, Apa John, will be grateful to them. Whoever takes care of it, may he make him worthy of the resting places in heaven.
And may he write their names in the book of life. Amen. So be it. [?]
The rich will honor the one who is rich in spirit by extending their hands in charity to the needy who share that same nature.
The poor will honor her who gave birth to the one who willingly became poor for our sake, so that he might make us rich in righteous deeds.
The slaves will honor her who bore the one who emptied himself, taking the form of a slave for your sake.
when they show their genuine service to their earthly masters.
But even more, let all of us together show it toward the commandments of our Lord.
We priests will honor her who gave birth for us to the priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek, by purifying ourselves.
As it is written: “Let the priests who approach God purify themselves, lest the Lord destroy some of them.”
We are also all the more afraid that we might be found closer to him here than everyone else,
but farther away from him there than everyone else because of our sins.
But all of us together, whether priests or laypeople,
Let us appeal and pray with all our heart,
so that she who can intercede for us before God more than all the saints may do so: the holy Mother of God, Mary, whom God has honored in heaven and on earth above all creation.
both things we see and things we do not see, so that she may intercede for us before her Son, the true God.
So that he may cover over the sins we have committed up to now with the vast ocean of his love for humanity,
and take this heart of stone away from us.
A demon, so that they too may inherit the fire and the worm with him.
They are laughing at him now [?] down in Hades,
all those who have gone down to him from the beginning until now, and those who will also go down to him until the end of the age, according to what each person's sins deserve.
What, then, is the shame of the devil and his demons, and Judas and all the sinners who will die in their sins without repenting, as they too laugh at one another
in the fire of Gehenna?
We want to understand that sinners are no different from one another—from the devil and his demons down in Hades, and the pagans and the heretics
and the barbarians and the Jews who do not believe in the Lord Jesus—for they are all alike in the fire and the worm that never sleeps.
Look at a place that is very deep and exceedingly wide, and take from every good tree,
from all the choice trees of Lebanon.
And every tree that grows on the earth, with whatever blessing [?], down to thorns and reeds.
And [?] all of them, and take from all of them and throw them down into the place that is dry and spread out, and set fire [?], while a wind
blows strongly behind them at God's command, and see how the appearance of their smoke and their burning differs from one another in what way.
For the wise already understand.
And they need nothing more from this example, because this is what those in Hades are like.
For they are in the midst of the flame, in the fire.
And they are under the worm that never sleeps. For God created the worm that is in Hades,
and the scorpion,
to be immortal,
just like the unquenchable fire that will punish the devil and his demons down in Hades by means of the fire that is never extinguished.
Likewise, we learned this through the accounts of the holy martyrs: he shows no mercy to any of those we mentioned.
As we found, he punishes them all and condemns them to death through such commands of his as are written in the accounts of the martyrs.
As it is written in his letters: "If such-and-such great bishops of the province are willing to obey my decree, which I have issued,
and worship the gods,
they will receive great authority, not only in their city,
but throughout the whole province.
But if they do not obey my decree," he said,
"and do not worship the gods,
they will be condemned to death." And this is how the holy martyrs endured until they received the crown of life.
We said these things because, if the king to whom God gave authority to rule over the earth
inspires such terror and displays such anger, with a great threat against those who reject his commands
and oppose his decree, so that he punishes them with swords and many other punishments, as it is written,
For the anger of a king is like the roaring of a lion, as he teaches godlessness and the destruction of the souls of multitudes,
having such a great threat at his disposal,
and an anger that cannot be appeased with money.
Then how much more the King of heaven and earth, the Creator of everything,
who created everything out of what did not exist—the heavens and the earth,
the sea and everything in it—will he not be angry?
Or can anyone restrain his fierce anger against every person, whether male or female, small or great, priest or monk, king or ruler, or any leader of a people
who turns away from the Lord's commands and his law, his ordinances, his judgments, and his testimonies, which he testified to us from the beginning through the mouths of his holy prophets
and through the mouth of his holy, only-begotten Son, Jesus, as the apostle says: “In many parts and in many ways, God spoke to our ancestors long ago through the prophets.”
But in these last days he spoke to us through the Son,
whom he appointed heir of everything,
through whom he also created the ages."

And again, through the mouths of his apostles: What, then, will happen to people like these? Or who will endure the fury of the wrath of God, the King of heaven and earth, who teaches true godliness, so that people do not worship wood and stones?
Like the kings who outlawed it, those whose fear and angry wrath we have spoken about.
These, in turn, teach people to worship wood and stones and all the rest
of the things made by human hands. But the Lord teaches people to worship him in spirit and truth, because he alone is the true God.
As it is written: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and truth.
And also to serve him, because he is the King of heaven and earth.
And he is the one who created them when they did not exist, whether angels, rulers, authorities, or all those in the heavens. For they all came into being through him.
Look, then, we have understood [?] that woe awaits every kind of person
who does not keep the Lord’s commands found in the holy Scriptures.
The kings we have spoken about, who withdrew from the truth,
punish bodies with the sword,
or with fire and other torments. But they cannot overpower the soul itself.
Nor will they see it.
Nor do they know where it is within a person.
Instead, it leaves unseen and goes into God’s hands, and he gives it what it deserves.
But God himself punishes both the soul and the body of those who disobey him together in the fire of Gehenna, which is in the underworld.
O you who alone are the true God,
and the Lord of glory, Jesus, we have nothing to say before you if you judge us and settle accounts with us
according to what our evil deeds deserve. But you will forgive for the sake of your name alone, because it is holy
and glorious forever.
Woe to everyone who neglects to leave sin behind until he dies,
as we have said many times.
What, then, have those who remain negligent until they die in defilement not harmed?
They have forfeited being warmly welcomed by the angels on the day of their visitation, when they would greet them with joy
and sing hymns with them with a voice of gladness and rejoicing, as it is written: “I remembered these things and poured out my soul within me.”
because I am coming through a wonderful tent
to the house of God, with a voice of rejoicing and thanksgiving, the sound of someone celebrating a festival.

And why do you trouble me?
Hope in God, for I will praise him. My God is the salvation of my face.
For indeed, according to the one who speaks through our father David, this is not about David alone.

As the Lord said in the Gospel, those who have guarded themselves will become like the angels in heaven, having put that age behind them while they were on earth and having done good deeds worthy of him.
And you have suffered loss, you whom we are speaking about.
