From this time onward.
You have also forfeited seeing the tree of life, so that you might take some of its fruit and [?]
just as the righteous and all the saints will eat from the tree of life. [?] prayer [?] of God [?] the righteous and all the saints.
That you will feed them from the tree of life.
And raise them in your holy first resurrection, with your apostles, your prophets, your righteous ones, and all your saints.
And you have lost the true rising in the first resurrection with the righteous and all the saints.
And your coming also in their honor and their glory with Christ.
And with his righteous ones and all the saints at the end of the age.
For indeed, there is no greater loss.
And there is no greater sorrow than that of those who died without abandoning sin or coming out of it before falling into the hands of Hades.
But I continue to speak sorrowfully about those among the dead who have gone down into it.
And those who
because of the good things he does for us, namely, his great patience in not destroying us,
we too who do evil on earth among those who do good in his sight.
But the time of harvest is coming, when he will gather the good into their resting place.
And he will also gather the wicked through the holy angels, to throw them down into Hades, into the fire of Gehenna, or out into the outer darkness,
the place where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
We ought to become wise, like all those who became wise through the abundance of the words of Scripture, as it has called us to repentance from the beginning.
If an animal is taught to walk from its youth, it does not change the way it walks until its old age, except through weakness.
But we have been taught the deeds of our salvation, or the deeds through which we will be saved.
Yet we, for our part, forget them.
Or if we have indeed instructed them at one time, but at another time do not watch over them—
If the rod is in the hand of the one driving the animal, and it is afraid, it goes along its way properly.
The words of Scripture are also more than a rod for a person, so that we may listen to them and continue in our conduct in every matter according to what pleases God.
Or does Scripture not say, “A whip for a horse,
and a goad for a donkey, but a rod for a foolish nation”? What is the rod for the foolish nation, if not the words of the Scriptures, as it is written:
For the one who brings wisdom out of his mouth strikes a foolish person with a rod.
Oh, this great sorrow that I am about to express! It is a disgrace to us who neglect to listen to God when he calls us,
“Come out of your sins and come to me with a few small good deeds done, and I will welcome you.
I will be a father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me,” says the Lord Almighty.
Is the snake not a vicious beast? Yet in a short moment, when the charmer charms it,
Wild animals of this kind abandon the wildness of their nature and acquire a gentleness contrary to their nature.
and come into the hands of the one calling him with great gentleness, because of the few words he heard from the mouth of the caller.
We too are those whose hearts have closed up, and we have not listened to all the words of the Scriptures—those of the Old Testament and the New Testament, and those of all the saints,
especially those of our holy father. They all call us to abandon the sins that are contrary to our nature,
because of which we will die, and to do good things in keeping with our nature, because of which we will be saved.
Yet we have not listened even now. Instead, we have become like a deaf snake that stops its ears and does not hear the voice of those calling it,
or a charm worked by a wise person, as the Scriptures say.
What must happen, then, before we come out of our evil deeds?
We are the ones who commit lawless acts, although we cannot endure the fury of God's wrath,
whom we constantly provoke by our evil deeds—especially we priests and monks who live in Christ's places.
Oh, how great will be the rebuke we receive on the day of our visitation, if we do not quickly withdraw from them!
As it is written, “The one who does not heal himself in his deeds is the brother of the one who destroys himself.”
“If a fool asks questions,” he said, “it will be counted as wisdom for him.”

Again, wishing also to honor [?] those who will abandon their sins and repent quickly, he says, “As for the one who provokes him by his own deeds, the name of the Lord is revealed in the greatness of his power.”
The righteous will be exalted by running to him, through the revelation of his love for humanity toward everyone who will abandon their sins and not return to them from this moment onward.
Or do you not know that it is a great sorrow before God for people to sin in his holy places, especially if they do not quickly abandon their sins?
If God said to Moses at that time, when he spoke with him at the bush, “Take off the sandals on your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground”—
although it was only a sandal—then how much more will he say to us who live in his holy places,

“Strip yourselves of all these lawless acts: defilement and pollution, theft and lies, envy and murders, fighting and rivalries, and all the other sins that are hateful before me, because the place where you live is holy ground.”
“And I dwell in it. My holy name has been invoked over it,” as he said through the prophet,
“Undo every bond of injustice [?],” so that we will have no words to say:
For even the commander of the Lord’s army, when he appeared to Joshua near Jericho, did not refrain from saying it to him.
“Remove the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground.”

To make clear again what we have said: it is not fitting for us to remain living in the places of Christ while disobeying his holy law. We must quickly tear apart the bonds of every lawless deed and cast them off ourselves,
so that the one in heaven will laugh at them.
And may the Lord mock them, speak to them in his wrath, and terrify them in his fury, so that the enemy
and his accursed demons may no longer persist in holding back or hindering those who want to leave their sins and repent quickly.
so that they may receive a blessing from the Lord and mercy from God our Savior,
and people may say, “This is the generation of those who seek the Lord and seek the face of the God of Jacob.”
Oh, how great is our reproach!
We are those who do not obey all these words until these five days in which we are living slip away from us.
And your lot will be with all those who have been disobedient from the beginning, abandoning the words of those who wanted their salvation and advised them to do what is good.
They paid no attention to doing it until they went down to the underworld.
If you do not know your lot, you who will die in your sins, especially in the places of Christ, we will tell you about it according to all the words of the Scriptures.
Your lot is the lot of Cain, who was the first on earth to receive a curse from the mouth of God because he did not obey his parents’ instruction.
Nor did he emulate the conduct and good deeds of his brother, righteous Abel. Instead, he prepared for himself an everlasting punishment from God.
Likewise, we too have not obeyed the words of the Scriptures,
so that we might turn away from our evil deeds and do good things, so that God would have mercy on us.

Nor have we emulated the conduct and good deeds of our righteous brothers with whom we live, until we have prepared for ourselves punishment and retribution that endure forever below in the underworld.
You are counted among those whom the Lord swept away in a flood of water in the beginning because they began doing evil from their youth.
And the earth had become filled with violence because of them, according to the words of Scripture, since they had not listened to righteous Noah as he counseled them.
He built an ark for the salvation of his household. Through it he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes through faith.

And as for what the text says, “Through it he condemned the world,” he did not condemn the world because they saw him building the ark, which measured three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high,
building it joint by joint [?], with one story, a second, and a third, and coating it on the inside.
and outside with pitch, and indicating to them that a flood would come upon the earth, having become a preacher of righteousness, as it is written.
And they did not obey him until they suffered death in indignation and wrath at the hands of the one whom they had angered, God Almighty,
and until this great destruction and annihilation came upon the earth.
There was no son protecting his father's body so that he could bury him, nor was there a father protecting his children so that he could cover them amid the waters of the rivers,
when the deep burst open and the floodgates of heaven opened. Nor were there women protecting their husbands,
nor husbands to cover their wives, nor brothers to cover brothers.
Instead, this one destruction came upon them all at once. Nor was there any memorial offering going up on their behalf to commemorate them,

or tears and mourning, with sacrifices being offered in remembrance of those who had died. Instead, they were all swept away in destruction, except Noah alone, who remained with his wife and his sons in the ark.
After he came out of the ark, he offered burnt offerings on the altar, and the Lord smelled a sweet fragrance.
He was pleased and established an everlasting covenant with him.
Likewise, we have not taken heed of those among the people of old whom he destroyed before us.
Nor have we envied our brothers who do good through hunger and thirst, through many fasts, through frequent nights of keeping watch,
through purity—the great main point we are discussing—through renunciation, and through all the good deeds they do.
bearing witness to their love for God, because he himself, the Lord, the good Savior, loved them even more, to the point of death.
indeed, death on a cross. While they do these things and the others, we watch them and live with them.
We paid no attention.
Nor did we listen when told that a destruction would come that is no different from the waters of the flood—I am speaking of death.
Just as the giants of old and all the people whom he destroyed were not permitted to see Noah
and his whole household, which was saved, so sinful people or lawless brothers will not be permitted to see righteous brothers in their rest
and their joy, when they die in their wickedness.
Again, you are counted with Pharaoh and his entire multitude, who drowned in the Red Sea,
because they disobeyed God.
As he spoke with them through the holy prophet Moses and Aaron,
You are counted among all those whom the Lord struck down in the wilderness with various kinds of death because they disobeyed him,
rather than doing everything he had commanded them, while they were traveling with the people of God at that time, whom God protected until he brought them into the land of their inheritance.
You are counted with the assembly of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, those for whom the earth split open.
They went down alive into Hades with their entire assembly.
Especially if you commit unlawful acts, defilements, impurities, and acts contrary to nature,
your inheritance and your allotted portion will be with the people of Sodom and Gomorrah.
You are counted with all those who plotted against the Lord Jesus until they killed him.
You are counted with those who rejected all the words of the prophets from the beginning.
You are counted with those who rejected the teaching of the apostles
and despised them.
You are counted with all those who denied the sound faith from the beginning, for whom no remembrance as blessed has come about.
You are counted with the pagans and the heretics.
You are counted with the bloodshed-loving barbarians, for we have not said anything that will not happen.
Our holy father, through whom God spoke, said in his holy letters,
For if a pagan, a heretic, or a blood-shedding Gentile turns to God,
God is more likely to accept him than this kind of brother who commits these abominations in his holy places, while bearing the holy name of God and wearing the monastic habit.
Or else, why do you not understand, you fools who are not wise,
that whoever dies in his sins
and is taken down to Hades is [?] different from all those we have mentioned?
For they are in Hades.
And he also told us this other thing in his holy writings.
For all the sinners who have died from Cain until now, and those who will die until the end of the age,
are taken down to Hades, as the gospel says.
Or does Scripture not tell us
that if God did not spare the ancient world, if God did not spare the angels when they sinned,
he did not spare those who walked with Moses in the wilderness at that time and leave them unpunished;
he did not spare the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah and refrain from burning them;
he did not spare false prophets and false apostles,
he has spared no one who sins in any way, from the beginning of creation until now, from being cast down into Hades.
just as the Scriptures bear witness to what we are saying.
Then will he spare us because we are clothed in a religious habit,
and because we have the appearance of godliness, while denying its power?
Will we say,
“What [?] in shame before our holy fathers and our holy brothers who have gone into God's presence, and all those who will go into his presence in holiness until the end of the age?”
Rise, and let us repent, brothers,
while there is still time,
so that we may attain what the Lord spoke of:
“An hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who will [?]”
